notes:
The list runs across two pages: n85.jpg (p.74) has 81-88 and n86.jpg (p.75) has 89-119. n83, n84 and n87 are not part of it. Columns: the number of years with returns out of 5; * where a return came for 1884; the station's number; the name and place; a Roman numeral for the light's class ('value and brilliancy'); the height in feet; the keeper. No light characters are printed, so character is null on every row. The class and feet are in 'other'.

Where the other reader's description is wrong:
(1) There is no Sanda. No. 105 is 'Mull of Kintyre', class VI., 297 feet. The station with no feet is 92 Ardnamurchan, which has class I. but no feet and no keeper.
(2) There are 31 rows from 89 to 119. That is 26 under 'Mainland, Skye, and Inner Hebrides' (89-114) and 5 under 'Isle of Man' (115-119).

Braces:
- 93 Hynish Signal Tower, Tyree and 94 Skerryvore, off Tyree share one brace. One returns figure (5), one class (II.), one height (150) and one keeper (T. Dawson.) are printed for the pair. Only 94 has the *.
- 84 Stornoway, 2 lights: two classes (II., I.) braced to a single height of 56.
- 86 Monach Isles: classes I. and II. and heights 150 and 62 are braced to one keeper.
- 81 Cape Wrath: two keepers are braced into one entry, 'W. Wither & H. Morrison.', kept as one entry like 'Messrs Black and Beggs'.
- 83 Butt of Lewis: two keepers on separate lines with no conjunction, 'T. Edgar.' and 'A.Thompson.' (no space after the A.).

Keepers:
- The Monach Isles keeper is printed 'J. Young-' / 'clause.' over two lines, which I've given as 'J. Young-clause.'. The notes on p.76 spell him 'Mr. Youngclause', so the hyphen is very likely only a line-break hyphen. Those notes also say he had moved to an East Coast station.
- 'Frazer.' (Rona) has a surname only.
- 'D.M'Culloch.' has no space after the D. On p.76 he is 'Mr. McCulloch, Kyleakin'.
- Rhu Stoir's keeper is 'Wm. Wither.', and W. Wither is also named at Cape Wrath. The notes call Rhu Stoir 'Stoir Head'.

Spellings copied as printed: 'Kircudbright' (for Kirkcudbright), 'Wigtonshire', 'Lochindaul' (Loch Indaal), 'Island of Ghlais', 'Rhuvaal', 'Skervuile', 'Dhuheartach', 'Chickens Rock' (no apostrophe), 'Tyree'. Kyleakin is printed with 'Ross', not Skye.

'Do.'/'do.' in place means the same county as the row above:
- 82 = Sutherland
- 111-113 = Wigtonshire
- 116-119 = I. of Man

The L.V. of Bahama Bank is in small capitals, '(l.v.)'. It is printed under Isle of Man with ? for class and feet. Langness also has ? for both.

Things in the marks that don't add up:
- 117 Chickens Rock and 119 Langness have a * for 1884 but their returns-in-5-years column is blank.
- 89 Rona has a * but '0' for returns.
- 88 Barra Head and 114 Little Ross have a * but '1'.
So the 5-year count may not include 1884.
- The text says schedules went to 'thirty-four stations' and returns came from 'fifteen'. The list has 39 numbers (81-119) and 17 stars.

Unsure: a speck before 109 Turnberry, which I read as a blemish, not a *; and a blemish on Monach Isles' upper 'I.'.

I couldn't magnify the scans; everything is read from the page-size images.
